headlines.title: Tishman Speyer Opens ZO Clubhouses to Amex Cardholders
headlines.summary: Amex Business Platinum cardholders can use Tishman Speyer's ZO Clubhouses in six cities starting Oct. 22 wiht no fee increase.

headlines.title: After a Streak Not Seen Since 2008, Bank Stocks Face a Five-Day Test
headlines.summary: Equity Insider News Commentary - The 24-member KBW Bank Index was on course Friday for a sixth straight weekly decline, which Bloomberg said would be its longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis. The index sat about 13% below its August record, in correction territory, even after the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results. This week the spotlight moves to regional lenders, card issuers and a trust bank, with a different name on the calendar almost every day.

headlines.title: American Express vs. Mastercard: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
headlines.summary: American Express operates as both a lender and a processor with premium positioning, while Mastercard scales globally without credit risk.

headlines.title: American Express Pays a Small Dividend, but There’s More to the Story
headlines.summary: American Express Company (NYSE:AXP) stands out in the payments world. While Visa and Mastercard mostly run the payment rails, American Express does it all: it operates the network, issues the cards, and handles the lending.

headlines.title: Did Strong Credit Quality Just Shift Amex Stock's Investment Narrative?
headlines.summary: American Express is facing enforcement actions from the Federal Reserve and the OCC after past deficiencies in detecting and reporting suspicious activity under its enterprise-wide anti money laundering program. Despite these compliance issues, investors are focusing on American Express's strong credit quality, reserve release benefits, and the Oakmark Fund's decision to initiate a new position.

description: American Express Company, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an integrated payments company in the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, the Asia Pacific, Australia, New Zealand, Latin America, Canada, the Caribbean, and internationally. It operates through four segments: U.S. Consumer Services, Commercial Services, International Card Services, and Global Merchant and Network Services. The company offers credit and charge cards and complementary products and services, including travel, dining, and lifestyle and expense management products and services; and banking and other payment and financing products and services, including deposits and non-card lending. It also provides merchant acquisition and processing, servicing and settlement, fraud prevention, and point-of-sale marketing and information products and services, as well as network services. The company offers its products and services to consumers, small businesses, mid-sized companies, and large corporations through mobile and online applications, affiliate marketing, customer referral programs, third-party service providers and business partners, in-house sales teams, direct mail, telephone, and direct response advertising. American Express Company was founded in 1850 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
